question: When was the Supreme Court of India established?A. 1947B. 1950C. 1951D. 1952 (RRB NTPC Tier I (18/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: C
B
A
D
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is B. 1950

Explanation:
The Supreme Court of India was established on 28 January 1950. It was set up under Part V (Articles 124 to 147) of the Indian Constitution. The inauguration was done by the first President of India, Dr. Rajendra Prasad. The first Chief Justice of India was Justice Hiralal J. Kania. The Supreme Court is the highest judicial body in the country and its decisions are binding on all lower courts. It possesses the power of judicial review, allowing it to strike down any law that violates the Constitution.

☛ First Chief Justice of India → Hiralal J. Kania
☛ Headquarters of Supreme Court → New Delhi
☛ Sanctioned strength of judges in Supreme Court → 34 (including Chief Justice)
☛ Provision for judicial review → Under Article 13

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution describes the provisions related to financial emergency?A. Article 148B. Article 143C. Article 360D. Article 72 (RRB NTPC Tier I (28/04/2016) Shift 3)
options: C
A
B
D
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 360

Explanation:
Article 360 of the Indian Constitution deals with the provisions related to financial emergency. It empowers the President to proclaim a financial emergency if the financial stability or credit of India or any part thereof is threatened. During such an emergency, the Union government can give directions to states regarding financial matters, including reduction of salaries and allowances of state employees. This provision is part of Part XVIII of the Constitution. Notably, a financial emergency has never been declared in India. Other options: Article 148 (Comptroller and Auditor General), Article 143 (Consultation with Supreme Court), Article 72 (President's pardoning power).

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article related to financial emergency → Article 360
☛ Article related to national emergency → Article 352
☛ Article related to state emergency (President's rule) → Article 356
☛ Maximum duration of financial emergency → Indefinite, subject to parliamentary approval
☛ Provision for reduction of state salaries during financial emergency → Article 360(4)
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद में वित्तिय आपातकाल से संबधित प्रावधान वर्णित हैं?A. अनुच्छेद 148B. अनुच्छेद 143C. अनुच्छेद 360D. अनुच्छेद 72 (RRB NTPC Tier I (28/04/2016) Shift 3)

Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 360

Explanation:

question: Which of the following states does not follow the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution which deals with the administration and control of tribal areas?A. AssamB. NagalandC. MeghalayaD. Tripura (RRB NTPC Tier I (28/04/2016) Shift 3)
options: D
B
A
C
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nagaland

Explanation:
The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution provides for the administration of tribal areas in the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. These states have Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) to manage tribal regions. Nagaland does not come under the Sixth Schedule. Instead, Nagaland has a special provision under Article 371A, which requires the state legislature's consent before certain central laws are applied in matters of religious or social practices, Naga customary law, and ownership of land and resources. Therefore, Nagaland does not follow the Sixth Schedule.

☛ Special provision for Nagaland → Article 371A
☛ Sixth Schedule deals with → administration of tribal areas and Autonomous Councils
☛ Powers of Autonomous District Councils → land, forest, water, social customs
☛ State not following Sixth Schedule → Nagaland
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा राज्य संविधान की छठी अनुसूची का पालन नहीं करता जो जनजातीय क्षेत्रों के प्रशासन एवं नियंत्रण से संबधिक हैं?A. असमB. नागालैंडC. मेघालयD. त्रिपुरा (RRB NTPC Tier I (28/04/2016) Shift 3)

question: Which of the following states has a Legislative Council? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (28/12/2020) Shift 2)
options: Himachal Pradesh
Assam
Andhra Pradesh
Madhya Pradesh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Andhra Pradesh

Explanation:
States with a bicameral legislature in India have a Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) as the upper house. Currently, only 6 states have a Legislative Council: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, and Karnataka. Himachal Pradesh, Assam, and Madhya Pradesh have a unicameral legislature, i.e., only a Legislative Assembly. The Legislative Council of Andhra Pradesh has 58 members, of which 1/3 are elected by local bodies, 1/3 by the Legislative Assembly, 1/6 by teachers, 1/6 by graduates, and 1/6 are nominated by the Governor.

question: By which of the following Amendments of the Constitution, Fundamental Duties of the citizens were added to the Constitution of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (28/12/2020) Shift 2)
options: 44th Constitutional Amendment Act
42nd Constitutional Amendment Act
86th Constitutional Amendment Act
69th Constitutional Amendment Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act

Explanation:
The Fundamental Duties of citizens were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. This amendment inserted Article 51-A under Part IV-A of the Constitution, listing 11 fundamental duties. It was based on the recommendations of the Swaram Singh Committee. Fundamental duties serve as a reminder to citizens that they have certain responsibilities towards the nation along with their rights. These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by courts.

☛ Fundamental Duties are covered under which Article? → Article 51-A
☛ Fundamental Duties are in which Part of the Constitution? → Part IV-A
☛ Which committee recommended Fundamental Duties? → Swaram Singh Committee
☛ How many Fundamental Duties are there? → 11

question: Who gave the idea of a constituent assembly of India for the first time? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (28/12/2020) Shift 2)
options: BR Ambedkar
BN Rau
M N Roy
Dr Rajendra Prasad
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is M N Roy

Explanation:
The idea of a Constituent Assembly for India was first proposed by M.N. Roy in 1934. He was a prominent revolutionary and political philosopher. Later, in 1935, the Indian National Congress formally adopted this demand. C. Rajagopalachari further advanced the idea in 1938. Ultimately, the Constituent Assembly was formed under the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946). M.N. Roy was the founder of the Radical Democratic Party and a key figure in India's communist movement. His proposal laid the foundation for drafting India's democratic constitution.

question: The English Language continued to be used for official purposes of the Union via section 3 of the Official Language Act which came into force in the year : (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: 1963
1965
1970
1960
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1965

Explanation:
The Official Language Act, 1963 received the President's assent on May 10, 1963, but came into force on January 26, 1965. Section 3 of this Act provided that the English language would continue to be used for official purposes of the Union even after January 26, 1965. This was necessary because Article 343 of the Constitution had originally allowed English to be used for official purposes for 15 years (1950-1965) while Hindi was declared the official language. After 1965, there was strong opposition from non-Hindi speaking states to the complete switchover to Hindi, leading to the continuation of English as a co-official language. The Act aimed to balance linguistic diversity and administrative convenience. Its Section 3 specifically ensured that no language imposition occurred and both Hindi and English would be used for official work until a consensus was reached.

question: Which article of the Indian constitution grants the right to equal opportunity in public employment ? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/01/2021) Shift 1)

Article 13
Article 14
Article 16
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 16

Explanation:
Article 16 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the right to equal opportunity in public employment. It is a fundamental right under Part III and ensures equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State. Article 16 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence or any of them. Article 15 prohibits social discrimination, Article 14 ensures equality before law, and Article 13 deals with inconsistent laws. Article 16 specifically grants the right to equal opportunity in public employment, with provisions for reservation (Article 16(4)), residence-based conditions (Article 16(3)), and exceptions for certain posts (Article 16(5)).

question: Which schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the list of states and union territories and their territories? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/02/2021) Shift 1)

solution:

question: Which of the following taxes are NOT collected by the union government? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: Custom duty
Profession tax and stamp duty
Estate duty
Excise duty
solution:

Explanation:
In India, taxes are divided between the union and state governments. Taxes collected by the union government include custom duty (on imports/exports), excise duty (on manufacturing), and estate duty (on property transfer). Profession tax and stamp duty are levied and collected by state governments. Profession tax is imposed on professionals and businesses within the state's jurisdiction, while stamp duty is on documents and transactions. The distribution of taxes is mentioned in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution. Therefore, among the given options, only profession tax and stamp duty are NOT collected by the union government.

question: Which of the following is NOT true regarding the President of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: He cannot declare national emergency.
He is the Supreme Commander of the defence forces.
He appoints the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.
The President is the first citizen of the nation.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is He cannot declare national emergency.

Explanation:
The President of India has the power to proclaim a national emergency under Article 352. The statement that he cannot declare national emergency is false. The President is the Supreme Commander of the defence forces (Article 53), appoints the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers (Article 75), and is considered the first citizen of the nation. The President is part of Parliament and the head of the executive. The emergency proclamation is made by the President in writing and must be approved by Parliament. This power is a key feature of the Indian Constitution, allowing the central government to assume extraordinary powers during threats to the nation.

question: Maintenance of International Peace and Security is the main purpose of which of the following Units/Organisations? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 1)

question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 76 निम्नलिखित में से किससे संबंधित है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 1)
options_hi: उपराष्ट्रपति की नियुक्ति
राष्ट्रपति की नियुक्ति
महान्यायवादी की नियुक्ति
महालेखा परीक्षक की नियुक्ति
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है महान्यायवादी की नियुक्ति

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 76 महान्यायवादी (Attorney General of India) के पद से संबंधित है। यह अनुच्छेद राष्ट्रपति द्वारा महान्यायवादी की नियुक्ति, उनकी योग्यता, कार्यकाल और कार्यों का प्रावधान करता है। महान्यायवादी भारत का सर्वोच्च विधि अधिकारी होता है और सरकार को कानूनी सलाह देता है। संविधान के भाग V में अनुच्छेद 52 से 78 तक संघ कार्यपालिका का वर्णन है, जिसमें अनुच्छेद 76 महान्यायवादी से संबंधित है। अन्य विकल्प: उपराष्ट्रपति की नियुक्ति अनुच्छेद 63, राष्ट्रपति अनुच्छेद 52, और महालेखा परीक्षक (CAG) अनुच्छेद 148 में वर्णित है।
